Dollar 600/ year for four/five years, subject to academic performance

Malayalee Engineers’ Association (MEA) of Houston, Texas, USA has announced scholarships for Kerala origin students to pursue Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Technology, Computer Science, Architecture or Naval Architecture studies, in a nationally accredited engineering college or university in India.
The students need to meet the following criteria to avail the scholarship:
Annual family income must be less than INR 1,50,000 per year.

Student must be enrolled in an accredited Engineering College or University for at least a 4-year (8 semesters) or 5-years (10 semesters for B.Arch) course leading to a Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Technology, Computer Science, Architecture or Naval Architecture as a first-year student in 2017.
Ranked lower than 5000 (1 to 5000) in the Govt. of Kerala Engineering Entrance Examination (KEAM Rank) or National Aptitude Test in Architecture (NATA) score greater than 110 (For B. Arch students)
Scored above 85% marks in Class X and XII examinations
Application procedure to apply for the scholarship:
Fill in all the required details.
Finally, send the application form through email at meahouston.2017scholarship@gmail.com.
Attach the scanned copies of the following documents with the 'Detailed Scholarship Form'.
Marksheets of Class X and Class XII Examinations attested by the Principal or Head of the Department of the Engineering College where the student is currently enrolled
Marks-list and Rank Certificate of the Govt. of Kerala Engineering Entrance Examination
Income Certificate including all sources, issued by Tahsildar / Village Officer.
'Recommendation Letter Form' completed and signed by the Principal, Headmaster or teacher of the school where the student studied for class X or XII.
If parents or guardians are daily wage workers or labourers or engaged in agriculture, trade or business, a statement explaining the type of work, labour, agriculture or business must be submitted.
Details of awards and honours received in extracurricular activities.
An essay by the applicant describing any financial difficulty or special circumstances that merit special consideration during evaluation of the application.

A statement providing details of scholarships, grants and non-repayable financial awards the student may be receiving from sources other than MEA Houston. Include amounts, duration of payment, source’s name and basis of award in your statement.
